{{Short description|Totality of intensions of an object}}
{{One source|date=August 2025}}

In [[logic]], the '''comprehension'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Logical inferences and comprehension: How mental-logic and text processing theories need each other. |url=https://psycnet.apa.org/record/1998-07490-004 |website=psycnet.apa.org}}</ref> of an object is the totality of [[intension]]s, that is, attributes, characters, marks, properties, or qualities, that the object possesses, or else the totality of intensions that are [[relevance|pertinent]] to the  context of a given discussion.  This is the correct technical term for the whole collection of intensions of an object, but it is common in less technical usage to see 'intension' used for both the composite and the primitive ideas.
